raw_record.support_text: The paper notes that concern over hepatic injury with CGRP-receptor antagonists came from findings with first-generation gepants that showed a possible correlation with elevated ALT/AST up to 3× the upper limit of normal, but states that both ubrogepant and rimegepant completed phase III trials showing efficacy and safety with no signs of hepatic injury.
raw_record.extra_details: Phase III efficacy/safety trials (ACHIEVE I and II, 25/50/100 mg for acute migraine) completed with no signs of hepatic injury, despite an earlier possible correlation of elevated ALT/AST up to 3x ULN seen with first-generation gepants.

raw_record.support_text: Drug-induced hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, muscle pain, or rhabdomyolysis was not observed in any of the patients receiving rosuvastatin (group receiving metformin plus rosuvastatin). No serious adverse event was observed, and only minor gastrointestinal complaints occurred in a few patients without treatment discontinuation.
raw_record.extra_details: In a 12-week trial of metformin versus metformin plus rosuvastatin (10 mg) in polycystic ovary syndrome; no hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, muscle pain, or rhabdomyolysis was observed in any patient receiving rosuvastatin. Minor gastrointestinal complaints occurred in two patients in Group M and three in Group MR, but therapy was not discontinued.

The treatment was low-dose pioglitazone (7.5 mg/d for 21 of 28 d) added to low-dose FluMet (flutamide plus metformin) plus a transdermal estroprogestagen.

raw_record.extra_details: Minor drops in serum ALT, AST, γ-GT, and lactate dehydrogenase (all P < 0.005) were interpreted as absence of hepatotoxicity; no clinical side effects detected. This negative conclusion is reported for the whole regimen, with pioglitazone being the added drug of interest.

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that ganetespib, a second-generation Hsp90 inhibitor that is structurally unrelated to geldanamycin-derived inhibitors, is not associated with significant hepatotoxicity, in contrast to the first-generation geldanamycin-derived agents whose utility was limited by hepatotoxicity.
raw_record.extra_details: Phase I dose-finding trial in previously treated advanced HCC patients; RP2D 200 mg/m² weekly for first 3 weeks of each 4-week cycle, with acceptable safety in Child Pugh class A cirrhosis; ganetespib is structurally unrelated to geldanamycin-derived inhibitors.

raw_record.support_text: In the EXPLORE-Xa trial, the oral factor Xa inhibitor betrixaban was compared with warfarin in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. Betrixaban at 40 mg daily caused less bleeding than warfarin, and at 60 and 80 mg daily caused similar bleeding rates, but no hepatotoxicity was seen in the trial.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Evaluated in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation with an additional stroke risk factor in the EXPLORE-Xa phase II trial at doses of 40, 60, and 80 mg daily.
raw_record.extra_details: No hepatotoxicity was observed in the EXPLORE-Xa trial. Betrixaban at 80 mg daily caused less bleeding than warfarin; 60 mg and 80 mg daily caused more diarrhea, constipation, and nausea than warfarin.

raw_record.support_text: In the same summary of the Wong et al. series, 33 similar patients were treated initially with methotrexate alone; resistance developed in 6 (18%), all were cured by actinomycin D, none required multiagent chemotherapy, and there was no hepatic toxicity. This is an explicit negative conclusion that methotrexate alone produced no hepatic injury in this group.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Methotrexate alone (without citrovorum factor) in 33 low-risk gestational trophoblastic tumor patients in the Wong et al. series.
raw_record.extra_details: No hepatic toxicity observed among 33 patients treated initially with methotrexate alone; this contrasts with the 6 cases of hepatic toxicity reported in the 68-patient MTX-CF group from the same series.

raw_record.support_text: In the efficacy and safety summary of the pioglitazone studies (as monotherapy and in combination with sulfonylurea or metformin), the authors report that adverse events included mild hypoglycemia, moderate weight gain and edema, and that there was no evidence of drug-induced hepatotoxicity or elevations in serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) in any of the studies. This is an explicit negative conclusion regarding pioglitazone and human DILI.
raw_record.extra_details: Three studies analyzed separately (studies 001, 010, 027), pioglitazone 15/30/45 mg monotherapy and combination therapy with sulfonylurea or metformin; intent-to-treat with LOCF; adverse events included mild hypoglycemia, moderate weight gain and edema; no ALT elevation observed.

raw_record.support_text: In a double-blind crossover study, Benson evaluated the therapeutic use of paracetamol in patients with chronic liver disease, comparing paracetamol 4 g/day for 2 weeks with placebo in 20 such patients. There was no evidence of hepatotoxicity, no effect on laboratory abnormalities associated with liver disease, and no evidence of significant paracetamol accumulation.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Patients with chronic liver disease; paracetamol at 4 g/day for 2 weeks under double-blind placebo comparison.
raw_record.extra_details: Double-blind, crossover study by Benson comparing paracetamol 4 g/day for 2 weeks versus placebo in 20 patients with chronic liver disease; no evidence of hepatotoxicity or effects on liver-disease laboratory abnormalities, and no significant paracetamol accumulation.

raw_record.support_text: Nine of the 68 primary-role DILI fatality cases died of chronic liver failure more than 26 weeks after DILI onset. Amiodarone, known to cause insidious fibrosis, accounted for one of these chronic liver failure fatalities.
raw_record.extra_details: Amiodarone is described as known to cause insidious fibrosis leading to chronic liver failure; it accounted for one of 68 primary-role DILI fatalities in the DILIN cohort, with death occurring more than 26 weeks after DILI onset.

raw_record.support_text: Two published cases of toxic hepatitis from citalopram are described: the first a cholestatic hepatitis with a histopathologic study that resolved 2 months after drug withdrawal, and the second a very nonspecific clinical picture without jaundice and with a cytolytic (hepatocellular) biochemical pattern that improved 5 days after withdrawal of the antidepressant. Causality assessment in the report applied the Naranjo scale (probable, 6 points), the CIOMS/RUCAM scale (probable, 6 points), and the María & Víctorino CDS scale (probable, 14 points).
raw_record.extra_details: Antidepressant (SSRI). Two published cases: case 1 cholestatic hepatitis with histopathological documentation, resolved 2 months after withdrawal; case 2 nonspecific clinical picture, no jaundice, cytolytic biochemical pattern, improved 5 days after withdrawal.

raw_record.support_text: Despite extensive clinical experience with halothane, hepatic necrosis is rare; it was estimated that only seven fatal cases of massive hepatic necrosis were associated with the first 5 million administrations. Retrospective studies revealed possible cases of drug-induced liver disease (8 in 14,685 administrations at Massachusetts General Hospital and 9 with one fatality at Presbyterian Hospital). The paper attributes hepatic injury to halothane as a rare, hypersensitivity-type reaction.
raw_record.extra_details: Halogenated general anesthetic (trade name Fluothane). Hepatic necrosis is rare: estimated seven fatal cases of massive hepatic necrosis in the first 5 million administrations; series of 15,747 and 6,618 patients without fatality; Massachusetts General Hospital retrospective study found 8 possible cases of drug-induced liver disease in 14,685 administrations, an incidence not exceeding that of other anesthetics; Presbyterian Hospital (NYC) found 9 possible cases with one fatality. Nonfatal anicteric liver disease considered a more common manifestation. Mechanism thought to fulfill criteria for a hypersensitivity-type reaction rather than true hepatotoxicity.

raw_record.support_text: In a prospective MTX study, adverse drug reactions reported with all doses of MTX (10-16 mg/week) during 24-week follow-up included hepatobiliary disorders and laboratory test abnormalities; the incidence of hepatobiliary disorders was higher for patients taking 12 mg and 14 mg/week than for those taking 10 mg and 16 mg/week. In the 52-week group the adverse drug reactions were similar, and the incidence of hepatotoxicity was high in patients receiving MTX 14 mg/week and 16 mg/week. Hepatotoxicity/ hepatobiliary disorders are thus attributed to methotrexate at therapeutic dosing.
raw_record.extra_details: Incidence was dose-related in the 24-week group (highest 16.73% overall ADR incidence at MTX 12 mg/week); in 24-week follow-up hepatobiliary disorder incidence was higher at 12 mg and 14 mg/week than at 10 mg and 16 mg/week. In the 52-week group hepatotoxicity incidence was highest at 14 mg and 16 mg/week, and GI and hepatobiliary disorder incidence was lower in patients concomitantly using folic acid (4.82% and 13.18%) than in non-users (8.33% and 20.83%). MTX doses used were 8, 10, 12, 14, and 16 mg/week.

condition_group: exposure=therapeutic_use+population=human+reported_condition=antecedent atopy and drug-hypersensitivity reactions; hepatitis occurred after a second (re)exposure to halothane in two of the three cases; one patient (patient 3) was diabetic with a fish allergy
condition_text: Antecedent atopy and drug-hypersensitivity reactions; hepatitis occurred after a second (re)exposure to halothane in two of the three cases; one patient (Patient 3) was diabetic with a fish allergy.

raw_record.support_text: The paper reports three patients in whom hepatitis developed in relation to halothane anesthesia. The authors conclude that the evidence supports the diagnosis of a halothane-induced sensitization reaction with hepatitis, based on the characteristic temporal relation between halothane exposure and fever/jaundice, onset with chills and high fever, significant eosinophilia, antecedent atopy and drug-hypersensitivity reactions, occurrence of the hepatitis after a second halothane exposure in two of the three cases, and histologic features consistent with drug-induced hepatitis. Biopsies showed severe hepatitis with bridging necrosis, and all three patients recovered fully.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Antecedent atopy and drug-hypersensitivity reactions; hepatitis occurred after a second (re)exposure to halothane in two of the three cases; one patient (Patient 3) was diabetic with a fish allergy.
raw_record.extra_details: Serial SGOT (normal 15–35 IU/ml) and serum bilirubin (normal 0.1–1.4 mg/dl) values were recorded after halothane exposure for each patient (e.g., Patient 1 SGOT 1600 IU/ml at 2 days, bilirubin 2.66 mg/dl at 7 days; Patient 2 SGOT 2480 IU/ml at 6 days, bilirubin 13.50 mg/dl at 13 days). Histology showed severe hepatitis with bridging necrosis and, in one case, granulomata and giant cells; Patient 3 had eosinophilia rising to 11%. The authors noted absence of epidemiologic or serologic evidence of type B hepatitis and excluded postoperative cholestasis or centrilobular necrosis attributable to shock/multiple transfusions. All patients recovered fully.

raw_record.support_text: Valproic acid is described as a known antiepileptic drug with an infrequent tendency to produce hepatic necrosis. In a study by Kassahun et al., 28 pediatric patients were evaluated, and patients who had developed liver failure due to therapy with valproic acid showed three to four times higher excretion of the mercapturic acid metabolite 5-(N-acetylcysteine-S-yl)-3-ene-valproic acid (up to 5.7 g/ml urine) when adjusted for creatinine.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Findings in pediatric patients (28 pediatric patients in the cited study); valproic acid also described as teratogenic and affecting the nervous system.
raw_record.extra_details: Synonyms: 2-propylpentanoic acid, dipropylacetic acid (Depakene, Depakine, Convulex, Epilim). Half-life 7-15 h depending on age; plasma clearance about 5-10 ml/min; undergoes enterohepatic circulation and is found in saliva, bile, feces, and urine. Reactive metabolite urinary conjugate 5-(N-acetylcysteine-S-yl)-3-ene-valproic acid found at up to 5.7 g/ml urine; ~3-4x higher levels in patients who developed valproic-acid-therapy-related liver failure; similar excretion difference seen for 2-propyl-2,4-pentadienoic acid.

raw_record.support_text: In this letter about the risks of isoniazid preventive therapy, the authors cite the U.S. Public Health Service Cooperative Surveillance Study, in which among 3227 young adults given preventive therapy with isoniazid, three per 1000 (0.3%) developed hepatitis that was probably associated with the drug. They also discuss the study by Byrd and colleagues, in which preventive therapy with close clinical and biochemical monitoring was started in 1000 patients (281 lost to follow-up), with no severe hepatitis detected; the authors argue that about 400 patients aged 20-35 are too few to demonstrate that close supervision reduced the hepatitis rate below three per 1000.
raw_record.extra_details: Population was young adults (only risk factor a positive tuberculin test) receiving preventive therapy for tuberculosis. US Public Health Service Cooperative Surveillance Study: 3 per 1000 (3227 persons) developed hepatitis probably associated with isoniazid. Byrd study: 1000 patients started, 281 lost to follow-up, no severe hepatitis detected in approximately 400 patients aged 20-35; authors note too few young adults to conclude close supervision reduced the rate.

raw_record.support_text: Sixty-four patients with colorectal cancer with liver metastases were treated with FUDR (5-fluorodeoxyuridine) infusions, 20 in a pilot study by hepatic artery infusion and 44 randomized to hepatic artery plus intravenous (IA/IV) versus hepatic artery alone (IA) continuous 14-day monthly infusion. Drug toxicities in the 64 patients included gastroenteritis (21%), chemical hepatitis (57%), and biliary sclerosis (25%), with no difference in toxicity between the two randomized groups.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Patients with colorectal cancer metastatic to the liver; regional hepatic artery (or hepatic artery plus intravenous) infusion chemotherapy, 14-day continuous monthly regimen.
raw_record.extra_details: Aliases: FUDR. Dosing: 0.2 mg/kg/d for the IA group, 0.3 mg/kg/d for the IA/IV group. Reported liver toxicities in the 64 treated patients: chemical hepatitis in 57% and biliary sclerosis in 25%; gastroenteritis in 21%. No significant difference in FUDR toxicity between the two randomized groups (P > 0.1).

condition_text: Patients with ischemic heart disease and implantable cardioverter defibrillators; long-term/chronic amiodarone administration; indications include ventricular tachycardia prevention and primary prevention of sudden death in heart failure.

raw_record.support_text: The paper notes that potential amiodarone side effects are numerous and often relate to longer-term exposure. In a summary of trials of amiodarone for primary prevention of sudden death, hepatic toxicity was seen in 1.8% (along with pulmonary toxicity in 2.9%, thyroid toxicity in 3.6%, and bradycardia in 2.8%) during 12 to 46 months of follow-up. In the VANISH study, the escalated antiarrhythmic drug therapy group (amio-refractory, on amiodarone) had significantly more treatment-attributed adverse events, including nonfatal hepatic dysfunction, tremor, and drug intolerance (51 events vs 22 events in the ablation group; P=0.002).
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Patients with ischemic heart disease and implantable cardioverter defibrillators; long-term/chronic amiodarone administration; indications include ventricular tachycardia prevention and primary prevention of sudden death in heart failure.
raw_record.extra_details: Hepatic toxicity reported in 1.8% of patients in a summary of primary-prevention trials over 12-46 months follow-up (with pulmonary toxicity 2.9%, thyroid toxicity 3.6%, bradycardia 2.8%). In the VANISH study, the escalated antiarrhythmic drug group (predominantly amiodarone, dose <300 mg/d in 88.8%) had 51 treatment-attributed adverse events vs 22 in the ablation group (P=0.002), including nonfatal hepatic dysfunction, tremor, and drug intolerance.

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that in approximately 25 per cent of patients treated with chlorpromazine some evidence of hepatic dysfunction appears, usually detectable only as abnormal liver function tests (bromsulphalein retention and elevation of serum alkaline phosphatase and cholesterol), while jaundice appears in approximately 1 per cent and is usually of short duration. It notes that a rare fatality during the acute phase of jaundice has been observed, in about 10 per cent of patients chlorpromazine hepatitis lasts longer than three months, and prolonged jaundice over many months has been reported. The paper further presents a case (jaundice >300 days, xanthomatosis, hepatosplenomegaly) and a summary of five cases of chronic hepatic dysfunction with xanthomatosis attributed to chlorpromazine therapy.
raw_record.extra_details: About 25% of treated patients develop some hepatic dysfunction, usually asymptomatic, detectable only as abnormal liver-function tests (bromsulphalein retention, elevated serum alkaline phosphatase and cholesterol); ~1% develop jaundice, usually short; a rare fatality during the acute jaundice phase has been noted; ~10% have chlorpromazine hepatitis lasting >3 months. Chronic cases developed a xanthomatous liver disease with prolonged jaundice (197 days to 30 months), markedly elevated serum cholesterol (up to 2,500 mg/100 ml) and total lipids (up to 9,000 mg/100 ml), xanthomatosis, hepatosplenomegaly, portal hypertension, and biliary cirrhosis; the syndrome was termed 'hepatohypercholesterolemic cirrhosis' by Beattie et al. Elevated circulating coagulation factors (prothrombin, proconvertin, proaccelerin) were demonstrated; acetate-1-C14 studies suggested enhanced hepatic synthesis of cholesterol and phospholipid. Present case: jaundice >300 days, severe refractory pruritus, xanthomatosis, persistent hepatosplenomegaly.
